instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the opened Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or any shell; do not run Python, bpy scripts, Text Editor scripts, Geometry Nodes exported scripts, or blender --background automation that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Do not install or run helper add-ons that auto-build the required result. Use only Blender native GUI tools, menus, editors, and built-in save/export commands. Bake Vertex Colors. `scene.blend` contains a subdivided plane mesh object `Surface` at the origin (size 4x4 BU, 30x30 subdivisions -> 961 verts, 900 quads) and an Empty `Ref` located at (1, 1, 0). Scene units are meters. There are no modifiers yet and no vertex-color attributes on the Surface. Add a Geometry Nodes modifier on `Surface` that computes a per-vertex `influence` field based on the distance from each vertex to `Ref.location`, stores it as a POINT-domain FLOAT_COLOR named attribute `Col` with R=G=B=influence and A=1 (a grayscale white-to-black vertex color), then APPLY (bake) the modifier so that `Col` lives on the base mesh and the modifier stack is empty. Formula distance = length(Position - Ref.location) influence = 1 - clamp(distance / 2, 0, 1) So vertices close to `Ref` get influence ~= 1 (white) and vertices at distance >= 2 get influence = 0 (black). Suggested node recipe 1. `Group Input` -> Geometry. 2. `Object Info` for `Ref` in RELATIVE transform space -> gives Ref.location. 3. `Input Position` + `Vector Math` SUBTRACT -> `Vector Math` LENGTH to compute distance per vertex. 4. `Math` DIVIDE (other input = 2.0, with clamp enabled) -> clamped ratio. 5. `Math` SUBTRACT (first input = 1.0, second = clamped ratio) -> influence. 6. `Combine Color` (`FunctionNodeCombineColor`, mode RGB) with Red = Green = Blue = influence, Alpha = 1.0. 7. `Store Named Attribute`: name = `Col`, Data Type = Float Color, Domain = Point, Value = the combined color; wire Group Input -> Store Named Attribute -> Group Output. 8. Ensure `Surface` is the active selected object, then `bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)` to bake the result. Save the scene as `answer.blend`. Requirements: 1. Mesh object `Surface` exists. 2. `Surface` has 0 modifiers (the GN modifier was applied/baked). 3. `Surface.data` carries a POINT-domain FLOAT_COLOR (or BYTE_COLOR) attribute named `Col`. 4. `Surface` has 961 vertices (unchanged from init). 5. Influence distribution is correct (sampled at three vertices): - the vertex closest to Ref.location (1, 1, 0) has Col.R > 0.85 - the vertex at (-2, -2, 0) has Col.R < 0.15 - the vertex at (-1, 1, 0) has Col.R in [0, 0.5] 6. Col is grayscale: for every vertex, std across R/G/B channels < 0.01. 7. Every vertex's R value is in [0, 1] (with small tolerance 0.01). Gotchas (Blender 4.1): - In a Geometry Nodes tree use `FunctionNodeCombineColor`, NOT `ShaderNodeCombineColor`. - After setting `GeometryNodeStoreNamedAttribute.data_type = 'FLOAT_COLOR'`, the active `Value` input is the RGBA-typed one (`socket.type == 'RGBA'`); resolve it by name + type. - `bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply` requires the object to be active and selected.
